terminal.description: A shell at the top of your workspace. Build every file into out with this command, then run the hut with java -cp out lanternquay.hut.Hut.

tasks.title: Keep the fares inside the tickets package
tasks.description:
In `lanternquay/tickets/Fares.java`, under `// Task 1`, write the package line for the folder the file sits in, `lanternquay.tickets`. Then write a class `Fares` with no word in front of `class`, so that only the tickets package can use it, holding one method, `static int fareFor(int age)`: under 5 travels free, under 16 pays 160 pence, and everyone else 320.

Check builds the file as the lesson's command does, calls `Fares.fareFor` from code of its own in the same package, for ages on both sides of 5 and 16, and tries to use `Fares` from another package, where Java must refuse.
nextSteps: Read the parts of the lesson about packages and about `public` against no word at all.
Write the package line first: it follows the folders, with dots.
Write the class and `fareFor`, which is called through the class's name.
Build the folder with the command in the terminal and read any error.
hints: A file's package line is the first line of code in it, and names the folders from the top of the workspace, joined with dots.
With no word in front, a class can be used only by code in its own package. `fareFor` is called as `Fares.fareFor(9)`, so it is `static`.
`package lanternquay.tickets;` then `class Fares {` with `static int fareFor(int age)` inside: `if (age < 5) { return 0; }`, `if (age < 16) { return 160; }`, `return 320;`.

tasks.title: Make the ticket usable from the hut
tasks.description:
In `lanternquay/tickets/Ticket.java`, under `// Task 2`, write the package line and a `public` class `Ticket` with two `private` fields, a `String passenger` and an `int pence`. Give it a `public` constructor `Ticket(String passenger, int age)`, which gets the fare from `Fares.fareFor`, and a `public` method `String line()` that gives back the passenger and the fare in the form `Morag: 320p`.

Check builds the file beside a `Fares` of its own, with fares of its own, makes tickets from another package and reads `line()`, and from the tickets package tries to change each field, where Java must refuse.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about what `public` opens up.
Write the package line, then the class with `public` in front.
Decide which parts the hut uses from its package: those need `public`. The fields stay `private`.
Build the folder with the command in the terminal and read any error.
hints: Code in another package can use a class, a constructor or a method only when it has `public` in front.
`Fares` is in the same package, so the constructor can call `Fares.fareFor(age)` with no import and no `public` on `Fares`.
`public Ticket(String passenger, int age) { this.passenger = passenger; this.pence = Fares.fareFor(age); }` and `public String line() { return passenger + ": " + pence + "p"; }`.

tasks.title: Print the morning's tickets at the hut
tasks.description:
In `lanternquay/hut/Hut.java`, under `// Task 3`, write the package line for `lanternquay.hut`, import `Ticket` from `lanternquay.tickets`, and write a class `Hut` with a `main`. For each person in the queue the file gives, `main` makes a `Ticket` and prints what its `line()` gives back, one ticket per line, in queue order.

Check builds the file beside a `Ticket` of its own, whose `line()` gives back text of its own, and runs `lanternquay.hut.Hut` by name, as the lesson's second command does. It reads the lines your `main` prints.
nextSteps: Read the parts of the lesson about `import` and about running a class by its full name.
Write the package line and the import above the class.
Copy the queue into `main`, then loop over it, making a ticket and printing its line each time round.
Build the folder, then run `java -cp out lanternquay.hut.Hut`.
hints: An `import` line names a class with its package, and sits between the package line and the class.
The two arrays go side by side: the name at position `i` belongs with the age at position `i`.
`import lanternquay.tickets.Ticket;`, and in `main`: `for (int i = 0; i < names.length; i++) { Ticket ticket = new Ticket(names[i], ages[i]); System.out.println(ticket.line()); }`.
